title: Assessment of in vitro kinase activity of LRRK2 immunoprecipitated from cells
author: Francesca Tonelli
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bw4bpgsn
materials: Immediately transfer the cell dishes to ice.
Scrape the cells on the dish using a cell lifter (Sigma-Aldrich CLS3008, or equivalent) to ensure all cells are detached from the dish.
Start the kinase reaction by adding the master mix to the immunoprecipitated kinase and transferring the Eppendorf tubes to the thermo mixer set at 30 °C , 1000 rpm, °C, .

steps.title: Transfect HEK293 cells
steps.instruction: At 60–70% confluency, for each 10 cm dish add 10 µg FLAG‑LRRK2 (or empty vector) DNA and 30 µL of 1 mg/mL PEI to 1 mL Opti‑MEM, vortex 20–30 s, incubate at room temperature 20 min, add dropwise to the culture medium, and incubate cells at 37 °C.

steps.title: Rinse and lyse cells
steps.instruction: Quickly rinse each dish with room‑temperature medium lacking FBS, pour off and aspirate all residual medium, add ice‑cold lysis buffer (1 mL per 10 cm dish HEK293 or 750 µL per 15 cm dish MEFs) covering the surface, and transfer the lysate to an ice‑cold Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Lysis on ice
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysates on ice for 20 min to allow efficient lysis.

steps.title: Clarify lysates
steps.instruction: Centrifuge lysates at 20 800 × g, 4 °C for 10 min; transfer the supernatant to new tubes kept on ice and discard the pellet. Lysates may be snap‑frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at –80 °C, but avoid more than one freeze‑thaw cycle.

steps.title: Determine protein concentration
steps.instruction: Measure protein concentration of each lysate by Bradford assay in triplicate according to the manufacturer’s instructions; ensure measurements fall within the linear range and dilute lysates in water if necessary (expected ≥2 µg/µL for near‑confluent cells).

steps.title: Normalize LRRK2 levels (optional)
steps.instruction: Run ~10 µg of each cell extract on SDS‑PAGE, immunoblot for LRRK2 and tubulin, and adjust the amount of extract used for immunoprecipitation so that the enzyme amount is comparable across samples.

steps.title: Immunoprecipitate FLAG‑LRRK2
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL ANTI‑FLAG® M2 Affinity Gel (washed 3× in PBS and resuspended as a 1:1 slurry, where 20 µL corresponds to 10 µL resin) to 1 mg of cell extract, incubate 1 h at 4 °C with mild agitation.

steps.title: Wash resin with high‑salt buffer
steps.instruction: Perform three successive washes:

substeps.instruction: Collect resin by centrifugation at 2500 × g, 4 °C, 2 min and discard supernatant.
Resuspend resin in 500 µL lysis buffer supplemented with 300 mM NaCl.
Repeat the centrifugation and resuspension two additional times.

steps.title: Wash resin with Tris buffer
steps.instruction: Perform two successive washes:

substeps.instruction: Collect resin by centrifugation at 2500 × g, 4 °C, 2 min and discard supernatant.
Resuspend resin in 500 µL 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5.
Repeat the centrifugation and resuspension once more.

steps.title: Final resin preparation
steps.instruction: Collect resin, discard supernatant, and resuspend in 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5 at a 1:1 volume ratio (e.g., 10 µL resin in 10 µL Tris). Keep on ice.

steps.title: Aliquot resin for antibody coupling
steps.instruction: Dispense 10 µL of the prepared resin into each ice‑cold Eppendorf tube (one tube per subsequent antibody‑coupling reaction).

steps.title: Couple anti‑LRRK2 antibody
steps.instruction: To each tube add 10 µg anti‑LRRK2 antibody (UDD3) and 20 µL Protein A/G Sepharose resin (1:1 PBS slurry, where 20 µL = 10 µL resin), incubate 1 h at 4 °C with mild agitation; include a control where UDD3 is replaced by pre‑immune IgG.

steps.title: Wash antibody‑resin complexes
steps.instruction: Perform three washes:

substeps.instruction: Collect resin by centrifugation at 2500 × g, 4 °C, 2 min and discard supernatant.
Repeat the centrifugation and resuspension two additional times.

steps.title: Immunoprecipitate LRRK2 from extract
steps.instruction: Add the antibody‑resin mix to 5 mg of cell extract per reaction, incubate 1 h at 4 °C with mild agitation.

steps.title: Wash LRRK2 resin with high‑salt
steps.instruction: Perform three washes:

substeps.instruction: Collect resin by centrifugation at 2500 × g, 4 °C, 2 min and discard supernatant.
Resuspend resin in 250 µL lysis buffer supplemented with 300 mM NaCl.
Repeat the centrifugation and resuspension two additional times.

steps.title: Wash LRRK2 resin with Tris
steps.instruction: Perform two washes:

substeps.instruction: Collect resin by centrifugation at 2500 × g, 4 °C, 2 min and discard supernatant.
Resuspend resin in 250 µL 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5.
Repeat the centrifugation and resuspension once more.

steps.title: Final resin suspension and aliquoting
steps.instruction: Collect resin, discard supernatant, resuspend in 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5 at a 1:1 volume ratio, then aliquot 20 µL of resin into each ice‑cold Eppendorf tube (one tube per kinase assay).

steps.title: Prepare kinase reaction master mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a master mix containing 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM ATP, and recombinant Rab protein; add the appropriate volume to each resin tube, optimizing kinase and substrate amounts and reaction time (pilot study recommended).

steps.title: Stop kinase reaction
steps.instruction: Add 4X LDS loading buffer to each reaction to achieve a final concentration of 2X.

steps.title: Elute LRRK2 from resin
steps.instruction: Incubate the reactions at 70 °C on a heat block for 10 min, then centrifuge through a 0.22 µm Spinex column to collect the eluate.

steps.title: Heat eluate before analysis
steps.instruction: Incubate the collected eluates at 70 °C for 5 min on a heat block prior to quantitative immunoblotting.

steps.title: Quantitative immunoblot analysis
steps.instruction: Analyse the reaction products by quantitative immunoblotting as described in dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bsgrnbv6, using the recommended primary antibodies for Rab phosphorylation and LRRK2 autophosphorylation.
